summary: An Android application with several exported components, debug mode enabled, and backup enabled. Application requests multiple dangerous permissions (Internet, storage, camera, biometric). Exported activities, a service, a broadcast receiver and a content provider are exposed without protective permissions, increasing attack surface.
attack_surface: Exported SplashActivity (no protection), exported AccessControl1ViewActivity (no protection), exported DownloadInvoiceService (no protection), exported ShowDataReceiver (no protection), exported ContentProviderActivity (no protection)
allowBackup enabled (potential data leakage via backup/restore), debuggable mode enabled (easily intercepted via debugging tools)
permissions: INTERNET, WRITE_STORAGE, READ_STORAGE, CAMERA, USE_BIOMETRIC, USE_FINGERPRINT, custom permission
top_risks: Unauthorized invocation of exported components (activities, service, provider, receiver) leading to data exfiltration or abuse
Exposed ContentProvider without permission allows arbitrary data read/write by any app
Debbugable mode can be exploited to intercept traffic or inject code
allowBackup can be attacked to exfiltrate app data via backup mechanisms
abuse_hypotheses: External app directs intent to SplashActivity to trigger malicious behaviour or request data
External app queries ContentProvider to read user pins or sensitive data
Attacker triggers DownloadInvoiceService to download data causing downstream data leakage
Backup abuse by restoring compromised backup onto victim device to steal files
recommended_next_steps: Remove all export statements or add <uses-permission android:name="..."> with protection for each exported component
Disable android:debuggable and set to false via build config
Set android:allowBackup to false unless explicitly needed
Use networkSecurityConfig to prevent cleartext traffic
Consider refactoring exported activity to use exported=false or permission mask
